title: recall.requested
description: Written to `outbox_events` in the transaction that created a NEW recall (createRecall, submitLabResults with FAIL, decideComplaint with RECALL) and published after commit by the outbox relay; not written when an existing OPEN recall was returned. The recall itself (status changes, recall_batches, tasks, BR-10 close when there are no tasks — together with its own notification.dispatch RECALL {event: CLOSED} outbox row, R59) is already committed synchronously — the handler only fans out: (1) notification RECALL {event: OPENED} to inspectors, all task holders and the source origin organization; (2) one notification RECALL_TASK {event: CREATED} per task to its holder; (3) publishes rating.recalculate {cause: RECALL_SOURCE, sourceId: recallId} when the source batch origin organization is of type FARM. Everything — notifications (1) and (2) with the notification.dispatch algorithm, and the outbox row of (3) — is written in ONE transaction that starts with the processed_events claim (envelope, R56), so a redelivered event creates nothing. rating.recalculate is a full recomputation, so publishing it again is harmless.

openedBy.description: recalls.created_by — the user whose request opened the recall.
